Riff Teams Up With Griffin to Power Automated Savings Across FSCS-Protected Banks
summary:
Riff, a savings agent that moves customers’ idle cash across a panel of FSCS-protected banks to access competitive interest rates, is partnering with Griffin to build its product on regulated banking infrastructure. 
Traditionally, customers looking to make their “lazy cash” work harder have to compare rates across banks, open accounts, transfer money manually and keep monitoring rate changes. Riff aims to take that effort away by automating the process of moving customers’ cash to banks where it can earn more, and bringing it back whenever they want it.
In this partnership, Griffin will provide the embedded bank accounts behind Riff’s offering: a hub account for each customer and a pooled savings account, serving as one of the panel banks on Riff.
Alongside giving customers access to competitive interest rates, Riff can also help them make the most of FSCS protection. The Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS) protects eligible deposits up to £120,000 per person, per bank, so spreading money across more than one bank can protect a larger total balance. Together, this makes Riff a new, hands-off way to manage cash where customers set their preferences once, and Riff does the comparing, moving and checking from there.
Beyond individual customers, Riff works with platforms, advisers and employers that want to offer their clients a better home for idle cash. Riff is building its product and progressing through the regulatory process. The launch with Griffin is phased and subject to regulatory approval.
Speaking on the partnership with Griffin, Oliver Butcher, CEO and co-founder at Riff  says “Savers shouldn't have to become rate-watchers to get a fair return on their cash. Riff takes that job away entirely, and building on Griffin means we can do it on infrastructure that's built for regulated money from the ground up."
He further adds “Griffin has been great. From the moment we were introduced - helpful, knowledgeable and responsive. The type of culture and output I hope my own business can mirror.”
Phoebe Wallis, Chief Revenue Officer at Griffin added, “Riff is bringing a new approach to managing idle cash, the kind of ambitious product we love backing. We’re pleased to provide the regulated banking infrastructure underneath it as the team builds.”

content: Savings agent Riff has partnered with Griffin to build its automated savings product on regulated banking infrastructure. Riff moves customers' idle cash across FSCS-protected banks to secure competitive interest rates and maximize deposit protection without manual effort. Griffin will provide the embedded bank accounts behind the offering. The launch is phased and subject to regulatory approval.

FSCS-பாதுகாக்கப்பட்ட வங்கிகள் மூலம் வாடிக்கையாளர்களின் ஐடில் கேஷ் தொகையை தானாகவே நகர்த்தி, சிறந்த வட்டி விகிதங்களை பெற இந்த சேவை உதவுகிறது. இதன் மூலம் வாடிக்கையாளர்கள் வங்கிகளை மாற்றும் சிரமமின்றி பலன்களை பெறலாம். ஒழுங்குமுறை ஒப்புதலுக்கு உட்பட்டு இந்த சேவை படிப்படியாக அறிமுகப்படுத்தப்படுகிறது.

title: UK Wealth Managers Face Heavier Workloads Than Global Peers, Avaloq Research Reveals
summary:
UK wealth managers are managing significantly larger client books while spending more time on admin than their global peers, according to new research from Avaloq, a global leader in wealth management technology and services.
The findings reveal the scale of the pressures facing UK wealth managers – and the potential opportunities that could be unlocked – as firms pursue growth and consolidation while responding to increasingly complex client needs.
Avaloq's wealth insights 2026 research, conducted among 480 wealth management professionals and 4,256 investors globally, finds that UK wealth managers serve an average of 82 clients, compared with 57 globally. This represents a client book approximately 44% larger than the global average.
At the same time, UK wealth managers spend a third (32%) of their working time on admin, compared with 21% globally. Almost two thirds (63%) identify administrative workloads as a barrier to spending more time with clients, while 40% point to insufficient automation.
The findings come as UK wealth management firms seek to expand, both organically and through acquisitions. While consolidation offers opportunities to increase scale and reach new clients, it can also create additional operational demands as firms integrate different systems, processes and data.
Technology is not yet relieving the pressure
Despite technology being the obvious solution, many UK wealth managers believe their firm's systems fall short. Only 28% say they are satisfied with their firm's technology, while 58% believe their organisation is moving too slowly on digital transformation, compared with 50% globally.
The research also reveals significant obstacles to delivering personalised client service. Almost two thirds (63%) of UK wealth managers cite poor internal collaboration as a barrier, while 55% point to limited client data analytics and 53% report difficulties accessing client data.
Suman Rao, Managing Director for the UK and Ireland at Avaloq, says: "UK wealth managers have bright futures ahead, but our research shows that they are also under considerable pressure and not always able to fulfil their full potential. They are managing substantially larger client books than their global peers, but spending a substantial part of their working time on admin. As firms grow they need to make complexity doesn’t grow too, because more often than not this means more administrative work, which can result in less time for clients.
“Technology has a critical role to play in addressing this challenge, but our findings suggest that many firms are not yet getting the support they need from their existing systems. Wealth managers should be able to access client information easily, work effectively across their organisations and spend more of their time providing advice. Instead, too many are dealing with fragmented data, manual processes and systems that add to their workload.
"The industry is consolidating rapidly, which can compound these challenges, because acquiring scale and benefiting from scale are two different things. As firms grow, they need to ensure their technology can support larger client books without placing unnecessary additional demands on their people. The decisions firms make about their technology today will shape how effectively they can grow over the next five to ten years and beyond, so it’s vital wealth managers are supported by systems that enable them to deliver the personalised service clients expect."

content: Avaloq research reveals that UK wealth managers face heavier workloads than their global peers, managing larger client books while spending more time on administrative tasks. The study highlights that British professionals handle an average of 82 clients and spend 32% of their time on admin. Lianlian DigiTech and Visa Advance Trusted B2B Agentic Commerce for Small and Medium-Sized Businesses
summary:
Lianlian DigiTech and Visa, a global leader in digital payments, today announced the next phase of their collaboration to advance trusted B2B agentic commerce. The companies have completed their first live transaction in Asia Pacific through Visa Intelligent Commerce Connect, using a tokenised payment credential designed specifically for an authorised AI agent. Also unveiled at the Singapore Fintech Festival, Lianlian DigiTech is also launching LianLian XCard, powered by Visa Intelligent Commerce, extending the collaboration into business spending and expense management. 
The latest transaction builds on an earlier live purchasing journey and shows how an authorised AI agent can complete a business purchase using a credential designed for agentic commerce. For small and medium-sized businesses, these capabilities offer opportunities to simplify routine purchasing and payments while retaining control over spending. Together with LianLian XCard, the developments can help businesses spend less time managing everyday transactions and more time focused on customers and growth.
From controlled purchases to agent-initiated payments
In the earlier transaction, Lianlian DigiTech’s AI agent, LoopX Pay, identified a purchasing requirement, evaluated suppliers, placed an order and completed payment within predefined spending limits and approval requirements. In the latest transaction, LianLian XWorker, an AI agent registered in the Visa Agentic Directory obtained an agent-specific tokenised payment credential through Visa Intelligent Commerce Connect and completed a live office supply purchase.
The new credential adds an agent-specific payment capability to the end-to-end experience. Together with agent identification and business-defined controls, it supports transactions in which businesses can determine what an authorised agent may purchase and how payment is made.
Bringing greater control to everyday business spend
From 18 November 2026, eligible clients can apply for LianLian XCard through LianLian XWorker. Designed to help businesses manage spending across teams and projects, LianLian XCard offers tools including card limits and transaction thresholds. Customers can also link their LianLian XPay wallet to enable authorised AI agents to make payments using LianLian XCard within business-defined parameters. Selected AI-related benefits are planned for eligible customers.
“As AI agents take on a greater role in commerce, trust will be essential to helping businesses adopt these new capabilities with confidence,” said Stephen Karpin, President, Asia Pacific, Visa. “Our collaboration with Lianlian DigiTech brings together Visa's B2B payment capabilities and Visa Intelligent Commerce Connect to support secure, controlled agent-initiated payments. This creates new opportunities for small and medium-sized businesses across Asia Pacific to simplify purchasing, expand their reach and focus on growth.”
“AI is creating new opportunities for businesses around the world. As agents take on more of the work behind commerce, from evaluating options and coordinating purchases to making payments, security, trust and control must remain fundamental,” said Tim Shen, Co-President of Lianlian DigiTech. “With LianLian XCard, we are also bringing AI-powered financial capabilities and global business payments closer to companies’ everyday needs. We look forward to building on this partnership and helping more businesses embrace intelligent commerce with confidence.”
Together, the next phase of the collaboration and the launch of LianLian XCard will give businesses more ways to manage purchasing and payments as AI becomes part of everyday commercial activity. Lianlian DigiTech and Visa will continue exploring applications across procurement, supplier payments and other B2B workflows, helping businesses pursue new opportunities as intelligent commerce develops.

content: Lianlian DigiTech and Visa have announced a partnership to advance B2B agentic commerce for small and medium-sized businesses in Asia Pacific. The companies completed a live transaction using Visa Intelligent Commerce Connect, where an authorized AI agent used a tokenized payment credential to purchase office supplies. Additionally, Lianlian DigiTech is launching LianLian XCard, powered by Visa, to help businesses manage spending and expense management through integrated AI tools and wallets.

Apicunia and PayPoint Partner to Extend European Payee Verification
summary:
Apicunia has partnered with PayPoint to bring its European Verification of Payee (VoP) service to PayPoint customers, helping businesses verify beneficiary details before payments are made.
 
The partnership builds on PayPoint’s existing capabilities, including multichannel payments, Open Banking, Confirmation of Payee (CoP), and API-led platforms by adding European VoP through Apicunia’s specialist technology. The service allows customers to verify beneficiary names against account details before initiating a payment. Checking payment details earlier in the process can help businesses reduce payment errors, strengthen fraud controls and avoid the disruption of discovering a problem when a payment is ready to go.
 
While CoP supports name-checking for UK payments, VoP extends this capability to payments covered by the European scheme, enabling customers to check beneficiary details across additional markets.
 

Gary Farrow, Founder and CEO of Apicunia, said:
“We’re delighted to be partnering with PayPoint. Bringing together their payment expertise and market reach with Apicunia’s payee verification capabilities creates exciting opportunities. We look forward to collaborating to bring new services to market centred on ‘Know Your Payee’, helping businesses understand who they are paying and transacting with greater confidence.” 
Simon Coles, Managing Director at PayPoint, added: 
“Our customers need simple, reliable ways to check that payments are going to the intended recipient. Combining PayPoint’s payments expertise with Apicunia’s specialist Verification of Payee technology will help customers identify potential discrepancies earlier and make payments with greater confidence.” 
The partnership marks an important milestone in Apicunia’s work to make payee verification accessible to more businesses.

content: Apicunia has partnered with PayPoint to integrate its European Verification of Payee service for PayPoint customers. The collaboration aims to help businesses verify beneficiary details before initiating payments, reducing errors, strengthening fraud controls, and extending verification capabilities beyond the UK market into European schemes.
